product_scope: Local inference is realistic for food candidates, visible-item detection, image quality gates, barcode/OCR, and semantic labels; it is not validated as the sole source of grams, calories, macros, or hidden ingredients.
supported_platforms: iOS and Android, with different hardware/runtime strengths.
pricing: Local inference has no per-photo API charge, but model download/storage, battery, engineering, telemetry, update, and support costs remain.
popularity_signal: Candidate maturity is represented by official runtime/model documentation rather than consumer app adoption.
recognition_behavior: Recommended local pipeline: blur/lighting/food gate -> crop/segmentation -> food detector/classifier -> optional VLM for candidate explanation/JSON -> nutrition database lookup after confirmation.
identified_services: Relevant local platform services: Apple Core ML/Foundation Models, Android Gemini Nano via ML Kit/AICore, Google LiteRT/LiteRT-LM, ONNX Runtime Mobile, ExecuTorch, MediaPipe, and MLC LLM.
model_or_provider_confidence: Model/runtime capabilities are taken from official documentation/model cards; expected food quality is a recommendation requiring SuperNutrition benchmark validation.
local_inference_evidence: Gemma 3n is explicitly optimized for phones/tablets and supports visual/text input; Apple Foundation Models supports image prompting on eligible Apple Intelligence devices; Gemini Nano supports on-device multimodal prompting on a limited Android device matrix. Core ML, LiteRT, ExecuTorch, and ONNX Runtime provide deployment paths.
portion_and_nutrition_method: No reviewed local VLM provides validated mass/nutrition calibration. Use masks, reference objects, depth/AR, second views, or user serving input to reduce uncertainty, then calculate nutrients from a versioned database.
static_findings: The local-model shortlist is not derived from consumer APK assets. It is a deployment recommendation based on official model/runtime documentation.
reverse_engineering_limits: Published memory and latency figures are not full app peak requirements; tokenizer, KV cache, preprocessing, runtime overhead, and device thermal state add cost. Commercial model licenses must be reviewed separately.
candidate_models: Gemma 3n E2B: strongest open mobile VLM candidate to benchmark, but roughly multi-GB package class. Apple Foundation Models: excellent iOS semantic fallback on supported hardware, but Apple controls the model and OS availability. Gemini Nano: easiest Android prototype where supported, but device coverage/quotas/version drift matter. SmolVLM-256M/500M: approachable Apache-2.0 open VLM baseline with ONNX components; 500M likely stronger, 256M easier. Moondream 2 0.5B: spatial/detection specialist candidate after fine-tuning; current 3.x is too large for ordinary phones. Qwen2.5-VL-3B: capable grounding/JSON candidate but the official 3B repository uses a research license and needs commercial licensing review.
mobile_runtime_support: Core ML: best iOS backend for a dedicated classifier/detector/segmenter and can use CPU/GPU/Neural Engine. LiteRT/MediaPipe/LiteRT-LM: Google-native Android/iOS route; LiteRT-LM is preferred over maintenance-only MediaPipe LLM for new multimodal work. ExecuTorch: strong if the team owns PyTorch export and backend testing. ONNX Runtime Mobile: concrete cross-platform route for ONNX models, with Android NNAPI/XNNPACK and iOS Core ML/XNNPACK. MLC LLM: useful text-LLM engine but not first choice for VLM production.
device_requirements: Use INT8/4-bit where quality permits. Small classifiers can target tens of MB and broad coverage; SmolVLM-class models need roughly sub-1-2GB runtime memory depending on variant; Gemma 3n E2B/E4B is multi-GB download class; Apple Foundation Models requires eligible Apple Intelligence hardware and system storage. These are planning anchors, not acceptance thresholds.
expected_food_inference_quality: Local VLMs can identify visible foods and return candidate JSON but will hallucinate ingredients and portions without food-specific fine-tuning/grounding. Dedicated classifiers/segmenters should be more predictable for common taxonomy classes; VLMs help with novel dishes and explanation.
unit_cost_estimate: No network unit cost per photo; calculate total cost as device storage/download + battery/thermal impact + engineering and model update infrastructure. Compare against cloud price using an experiment with the same images and outputs.
privacy_and_compliance: Local-first processing reduces photo transfer and simplifies retention, but faces/interiors/metadata can still remain on device. Provide deletion/export, avoid logging raw images, and disclose Apple/Google system-model terms and device eligibility.
recommendation: Prototype three local tracks: iOS Core ML classifier/segmenter plus Foundation Models fallback; Android LiteRT classifier plus Gemini Nano on supported devices; cross-platform SmolVLM-256M via ONNX Runtime Mobile. Benchmark Gemma 3n E2B only on a high-end-device tier. Keep cloud fallback for ambiguous cases.
